the-big-picture/our-values: four values that shape how we work with clients, with each other and on the work itself. our values aren't just statements on a wall. they shape how we work day to day, define our culture and guide where we're heading. they're also part of how we grow: our capability frameworks use them to describe what good looks like at every level. constantly curious. there are no guessing games here. just curious people, with curious minds, asking the right questions so we can dig deeper into our clients' biggest problems and unearth their biggest opportunities. we're curious about ourselves too. we ask the team for feedback often, and we act on what we hear. stay classy. egos can get messy, so we leave ours at the door. there's only one thing that matters more than our work: respect. that's true for clients, for the work, and for the people we sit alongside every day. it's simple. just be kind. love mondays. we love coming to work because we actually love what we do. pair that joy with real ambition and you get some pretty unbelievable results. blow things up. we don't have to do things the way they've always been done. if something doesn't make sense, we blow it up and start again. because we can. it's why we've tried bold ideas of our own, like advanced leave and a progressive approach to parental leave. where they come from brothers joe and tom frazer, and their childhood friend will harms, started half dome in 2017 to unlock the power of marketing to transform businesses. they believed in the power of human potential. the name comes from the granite rock face in yosemite. the founders joked about starting a business together while camping beneath it on a road trip, years before the agency existed. it was meant to be a placeholder. it stuck. quote from your guide to half dome: we believe in empowering our employees and clients to achieve their whole potential, and we are committed to creating a space where challengers thrive. living the values - in your first weeks, your buddy will show you how the values come to life day to day. - in your growth, the values sit inside our capability frameworks, so they're part of every review conversation. - spot someone living a value? give them a shoutout in hibob.

the policy wording, summarised from the leave policy. your entitlements also come from the national employment standards and victorian law. annual leave permanent full-time team members get four weeks of base leave for each year of service. it builds up progressively from your first day, based on your ordinary hours, and carries over from year to year. part-time team members get it pro rata. half dome doesn't pay leave loading. you and your manager keep an eye on your balance together. if you have more than eight weeks saved up, half dome may ask you to take some. when that happens you won't be asked to go below six weeks, the period will be at least a week, and you'll get at least eight weeks' notice. half dome may close the office for a short period, usually over christmas and new year, and you'll be expected to use annual leave for those days. in your first 12 months you may sometimes take more leave than you've accrued, with your manager's approval. if you leave before you've built it up, the advance is deducted from your final pay. advanced leave after 12 months with us, you can take more annual leave than you've accrued. it's requested and approved like any other leave, with sign-off from your line manager and a partner from your department. it's paid as annual leave, so your balance may show as negative. advanced leave can't be used during a notice period, and any remote working plans need to be agreed alongside it. whole potential days each year you get six whole potential days: paid days on top of all other leave, for a long weekend or a shorter week. they're used leave-and-flexibility/how-to-apply-for-l: talk to your manager, get sign-off, then request it in hibob. here's the detail, plus a planner that works out the dates for you. the short version: - talk to your manager first. leave is agreed together, with workload and the team in mind. - your manager gets sign-off from your partner or head of department. - then request it in hibob with the right dates and type of leave. - plan ahead: four weeks' notice for planned leave, three months for long service leave. this page has a leave planner that counts working days and the date to get leave approved by. step by step step: talk it through with your manager. planned leave is agreed between you and your manager, taking into account the team's workload, how the work will be covered and what you need. step: get sign-off. your manager takes the request to your partner or head of department for approval. step: request it in hibob. once it's approved, add a leave request in hibob for the right dates and the right type of leave. hibob keeps the official record on your profile. checking your balance your available annual leave is on your payslip under entitlements, and in your leave balance in hibob. managers also see a quarterly leave report for their department, so they can help you plan time off. if you're sick or can't come in - tell your manager directly, and by talking to them , as soon as you can. give an idea of how long you'll be away if you know. - for two days in a row, or a day either side of a public holiday, you may be asked for a medical certificate or a statutory declaration. - attach it to your leave request in hibob. christmas and new year half dome may close the office for a short period, usually over christmas and new year. you'll hear about close-down dates well in advance, and you'll be expected to use annual leave for those days. this page shows a countdown to the next victorian public holiday. questions people ask q: can i take leave before i've built it up? in your first 12 months, sometimes. talk to your manager first. if you leave before you've accrued it, the advance is deducted from your final pay. after 12 months you can use advanced leave /topics/leave-and-flexibility/advanced-leave . q: what if i need leave at short notice? talk to your manager straight away. the four-week guide applies to leave you can plan; it doesn't apply to things you couldn't have seen coming. q: can i take leave during my notice period? advanced leave can't be used during a notice period. for anything else, talk to your manager and people and culture.
leave-and-flexibility/whole-potential-da: six extra paid days a year, on top of all your other leave, for a long weekend or a shorter week. the short version: - you get 6 whole potential days a year. they're paid, and they're on top of all your other leave. - use 2 each trimester . they don't roll over. - take them one at a time , not joined to each other or to other leave. - talk to your manager, then request them in hibob as “whole potential days”. this page has a tracker for this trimester’s two whole potential days. why we have them we want everyone at half dome to find a balance between work and life, with regular time off to rest and recharge. whole potential days build that in. they're paid days, in addition to all your other leave entitlements. how they work - use them for a long weekend or a shorter working week. - you get two each trimester. unused days don't carry over to the next one. - they can't be taken together, or joined on to other leave such as annual leave. - joining part-way through a trimester? you get a pro-rata share, based on your start date. how to book one step: talk to your manager. check your plans don't clash with anyone else's leave, and think about busy or peak periods for your team and clients. step: request it in hibob. choose “whole potential days” as the leave type so your manager can approve it. like other planned leave, aim to have it approved four weeks ahead. step: add it to your calendar. invite anyone it affects. there's no need to include the whole team. for managers note new starters : before you approve a whole potential day for someone in their first trimester, check their pro-rata entitlement with people and culture. questions people ask q: can i take both days together for a four-day weekend? no. whole potential days are taken one at a time, which spreads the rest across the trimester. q: can i add one to my annual leave? no. they can't be joined to other leave entitlements, so book them as stand-alone days. q: what happens if i don't use them? they lapse at the end of the trimester. two new days arrive at the start of the next one. q: how much notice do i need to give? the leave policy asks for planned leave to be approved at least four weeks ahead where you can. for a single day, talk to your manager as early as possible so your team can plan around it.
hiring-and-onboarding/your-first-90-days: everything to do, read and set up in your first three months, with a checklist that keeps track for you. welcome to the team. we're glad you're here. you'll find we're a team of smart, caring, driven challengers, and you'll soon see that you are central to our success. this checklist walks you through your first three months, from the week before you start to your probation conversation. tick things off as you go. the new starter checklist: before day one the week before you start : - say hello to your buddy: they’ll email to introduce themselves and tell you what to expect. - check your details in hibob: your employment terms and position description live there. - read our story: who started half dome, what we do and why it matters. week one days 1 to 5 : - coffee or lunch with your buddy: your buddy takes you out on your first day to say hello properly. - get to know our values: four short statements that shape how we work. - learn how we communicate: slack for quick questions, email for detail, a call for anything sensitive. - set up your tools: slack, hibob and everything else you’ll use every day. - read the code of conduct: how we treat each other, our clients and our work. first month weeks 2 to 4 : - weekly catch-ups with your buddy: a regular check-in for anything on your mind. - understand your leave: annual leave, personal leave and how to request it. - plan a whole potential day: six extra paid days a year, two each trimester. - choose your key for the trimester: journey, wellness or growth, worth $250 each trimester. - set up one-on-ones with your manager: agree how often you’ll meet and what you’ll cover. first 90 days months 2 and 3 : - fortnightly buddy check-ins: until you reach three months. after that, they’re still there when you need them. - set your goals: agree what success looks like in your role. - know where to get support: uprise gives you confidential support, coaching and wellness resources. - have your probation conversation: a chance to look back on your first few months with your manager. your buddy before you start, we'll match you with a buddy: a half domer in a similar role, usually in a different team. they're not your manager. they're someone to ask the questions you might not want to ask anyone else, from where to get a good coffee to how advanced leave works. - before day one: an intro email. your buddy says hello and lets you know what to expect. - day one: coffee or lunch. they meet you in person and take you out. - first month: weekly catch-ups. a regular check-in, plus slack or email any time in between. - months two and three: fortnightly catch-ups. until you reach three months. after that, they're still there whenever you need them. how we talk to each other - slack for quick questions and working together in real time. expect a reply within an hour unless someone's status says otherwise. - email for anything long, detailed or worth keeping. expect a reply within a day. - a call or a chat in person for anything sensitive, tricky or emotional, or anything urgent. - hibob for people news, like birthdays, work anniversaries, promotions and shoutouts.
diversity-equity-and-inclusion/acknowled: we work and thrive on the land of the wurundjeri people of the kulin nation. this is how we acknowledge it. our acknowledgement: at half dome, we respectfully acknowledge all first nation peoples on the beautiful land upon which we work and thrive, the wurundjeri people of the kulin nation. we pay our respects to elders both past and present and stand together with indigenous leaders for today and tomorrow, acknowledging this land was, is and always will be aboriginal land. our commitment in the spirit of reconciliation, we recognise the continued connection and contribution to nurturing this land, its waterways, and community. we aspire to value the perspectives of the oldest surviving cultures in the world and promise to respect and honour it, striving to learn from and cherish the deep wisdom and enduring traditions of the aboriginal peoples. we are committed to fostering a culture of inclusivity, understanding, and mutual respect, in the spirit of the wurundjeri people. this respect extends to all indigenous australians, whose resilience, strength and deep connection to the country inspires us, and provides direction for our own journey. just as we seek to unlock potential in the world of media, we strive to embrace the rich history and vibrant culture of the indigenous peoples, and a vital part of our shared australian identity. we commit to ongoing education and positive, intentional actions to unlock this shared understanding in society, in support of the aboriginal peoples. we are immensely privileged to share this land and uphold the values of its traditional custodians. as we move forward, we will continue to learn, grow and make strides in our efforts to support and champion indigenous voices within our agency, industry, and community. using it - open client presentations, pitches and events with the short acknowledgement above. - cultural, ceremonial or religious observance leave and public holiday swaps are there if you need them. see cultural and religious leave /topics/diversity-equity-and-inclusion/cultural-and-religious-leave .
